papers.title: C3a receptor signalling in ObRb-expressing neurons promotes leptin resistance and obesity-associated cardiac remodelling
papers.summary: Obesity is associated with hypothalamic inflammation, leptin resistance and increased cardiometabolic risk, but the neuroimmune signals linking nutrient excess to these outcomes remain incompletely defined. Here we show that diet-induced obesity is accompanied by local complement activation in the mouse hypothalamus, leading to C3a generation that signals through C3a receptor (C3aR) on leptin receptor (ObRb)-expressing neurons and blunts leptin signaling. Deletion of C3aR in ObRb-expressing neurons preserves leptin responsiveness, reduces food intake and weight gain, and improves glucose homeostasis during dietary challenge. Systemic pharmacological C3aR targeting induces weight loss and improves leptin responsiveness in established obesity. papers.title: Mesaconic acid delivery via biomaterials and engineered probiotics to the gut reduces inflammation in Crohn's Diseases mouse models
papers.summary: Mesaconate (MES, an immunosuppressive metabolite) but not itaconate is upregulated in stool of Crohns Disease (CD) patients, albeit below therapeutic levels.. However, colonic MES level is difficult to maintain because of its high absorption rate, limiting its therapeutic potential for CD. Herein, we developed two strategies that elevate MES level and suppress inflammation: EcN-CAD, an engineered probiotic Escherichia coli Nissle 1917 (EcN) that overexpresses cis-aconitate decarboxylase (CAD, produces itaconic acid that is converted to MES); and MES+Zn, a Zinc-MES ionically crosslinked formulation. Mechanistically, MES modulates T cell function by downregulating glycolytic and mitochondrial activity and decrease ROR{gamma}t expression. In preclinical SAMP1/YitFC dexamethasone-withdrawal model and TNFDARE model, MES+Zn decreased gut permeability significantly compared to controls and reduced myeloperoxidase (MPO, an inflammatory marker) 1000-fold compared to controls. papers.title: Human CD4 T cells coordinate antitumor immunity through indirect antigen presentation
papers.summary: Whether human tumor-specific CD4 T cells can drive antitumor immunity in cancers lacking tumor-cell MHC class II expression has not been established. In MHC class II-negative melanoma and breast cancer, CD4 T cells with a transcriptional signature of tumor specificity correlated with myeloid and CD8 T cell activation. Using a patient-derived NY-ESO-specific, HLA-DP04-restricted TCR, we tested whether human CD4 T cells could control tumors through indirect antigen presentation. In vitro, CD4 T cells inhibited HLA-DP-negative melanoma growth through recognition of tumor-derived antigen on antigen presenting cells (APC). In humanized mice, CD4 T cell transfer induced regression of HLA-DP-negative tumors, and control required HLA-matched human APCs. CD4 T cell transfer induced endogenous CD8 T cell proliferation and myeloid activation that mirrored immune programs correlated with the presence of these cells in patients. papers.title: Crystal structure of activated MAPKAPK2 kinase reveals a C-lobe allosteric pocket for furan-2-carboxamide inhibitors
papers.summary: MAPK-activated protein kinase 2 (MAPKAPK2, MK2) is a downstream substrate of p38 MAPK that regulates inflammatory signaling and cytokine synthesis, making it an attractive therapeutic target. Although several crystal structures of MAPKAPK2 with ATP-competitive inhibitors have supported drug discovery, structural elucidation of selective non-ATP-competitive inhibitors has remained challenging. MK-25 is a non-ATP-competitive furan-2-carboxamide MAPKAPK2 inhibitor developed at Merck to overcome the selectivity and cellular-efficacy limitations of ATP-competitive chemotypes. Here, we show through isothermal titration calorimetry that MK-25 binds the activated MAPKAPK2, consistent with state-dependent allosteric binding. To determine the binding mode of MK-25, we solved a 2.8 A resolution crystal structure of an activated MAPKAPK2 construct in ternary complex with the ATP-site inhibitor PF-3644022 and a bromo-analogue of MK-25. papers.title: Differential Effects of Distinct Type I Interferons and IFN Inducers on Fc Receptor landscape and myeloid cell function
papers.summary: Antiviral monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) rely on Fc-mediated effector functions, which depend on interactions with Fc receptors (FcRs) expressed on immune cells such as monocytes and dendritic cells (DCs). While combinations of antiviral mAbs with type I interferons (IFN-I) or IFN inducers are being explored to enhance therapeutic efficacy, the impact of these immunomodulators on FcR expression remains poorly understood. In this study, we investigated the effects of IFN-2, IFN-{beta}, and the IFN-inducer TAK-981 (a SUMOylation inhibitor) on FcR modulation and functional activation in human monocyte subsets and monocyte-derived DCs (moDCs). Using flow cytometry and imaging techniques, we mapped the expression of activating Fc{gamma}Rs (CD64, CD32A, CD16A) and neonatal FcR (FcRn) under steady-state and stimulated conditions. papers.title: C1q-mediated steric hindrance limits FcγR contribution to antibody-driven phagocytosis by human neutrophils
papers.summary: Phagocytosis and killing of bacteria by neutrophils is a key driver of human immunity against invading infections. IgG antibodies targeting the bacterial surface can potently enhance phagocytic uptake by engaging Fc gamma receptors (Fc{gamma}Rs) on the neutrophil membrane. In addition, IgG-mediated complement activation triggers surface deposition of complement opsonins that engage complement receptors (CRs) to further enhance target cell clearance. In this paper, we reveal that complement deposition prevents engagement of Fc{gamma}Rs to the Fc-domain of surface-bound IgG molecules. When complement is present, we observe that blockade of Fc{gamma}Rs does not influence phagocytosis of both Gram-positive and -negative bacteria (using Staphylococcus aureus and Klebsiella pneumoniae as model organisms). papers.title: Host Metabolic Reprogramming Defines Macrophage Antifungal Activity Against Cryptococcus neoformans
papers.summary: Innate immune cells, including macrophages and DCs, are critical for controlling infection by Cryptococcus neoformans. Although C. neoformans is phagocytosed equally by each pulmonary phagocyte subset, CD11b+ DCs support fungal growth, whereas Ly6c- monocyte-like macrophages are antifungal. The metabolic programs underlying these contrasting responses remain incompletely understood, but our previous work points to increased glycolysis in antifungal cells. Therefore, we hypothesized that metabolic reprogramming in phagocytes following cryptococcal exposure leads to different outcomes. We examined ten metabolic pathways using flow cytometry, metabolic inhibition, antifungal assays, and pulmonary infection. papers.title: Efficiency of a Multi-step Screening and Enrichment Process for Prospective Sepsis Cohort Enrollment
papers.summary: Background: Host response and biomarker research to advance sepsis therapeutics requires well-characterized cohorts with longitudinal biospecimens across a range of hosts and infections. Automated screening based on SIRS criteria is sensitive but nonspecific and identifies more candidates than research teams can approach, sample, and follow longitudinally. We evaluated a structured enrichment review by non-physician study staff, done after automated screening in a hospital-wide prospective sepsis cohort. Methods: The CISID cohort is a prospective observational study of hospitalized patients with suspected sepsis, enrolling adults from the ED, inpatient wards, and ICUs at a tertiary academic medical center. papers.title: Community knowledge, chronic morbidity and microfilaraemia following mass drug administration for lymphatic filariasis in northern Ghana: a cross-sectional study
papers.summary: Objectives To assess microfilaraemia, chronic lymphatic filariasis (LF)-related morbidity, and community knowledge and self-reported preventive behaviours in a rural community in northern Ghana following prolonged mass drug administration (MDA). Design Community-based cross-sectional study. Setting Birifor community, Lawra Municipality, Upper West Region, northern Ghana, from October 2024 to January 2025. Participants A total of 261 community members aged 10 years and above were selected using random sampling and participated in the study. Outcome measures Outcome measures included microfilaraemia detected by night blood microscopy, chronic LF-related morbidity identified through clinical examination, and community knowledge and self-reported preventive behaviours assessed using a structured questionnaire. papers.title: Temporal and Phylodynamic analyses of the 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo
papers.summary: The Democratic Republic of the Congo is experiencing a major outbreak of Ebola disease caused by Orthoebolavirus bundibugyoense (Bundibugyo virus), which was declared on May 15, 2026. To investigate the timing of emergence and early transmission, we generated near full length Bundibugyo virus genomes from 686 PCR-confirmed individuals across 22 health zones. We estimated the time of emergence as late February 2026 (95% highest posterior density interval [HPDI]: January 21 and March 25, 2026) and an evolutionary rate of 8.7X10-4 substitutions per site per year (95% HPDI: 7.6 and 9.9X10-4), with no evidence of mutations associated with rapidly growing lineages.

papers.title: Transitions to Comfort Measures Only Among Patients Hospitalized With Sepsis: Clinical Drivers and Implications for Mortality
papers.summary: Background Mortality in sepsis is often considered a direct consequence of infection and organ dysfunction, although many deaths occur after withdrawal of life sustaining treatment. The clinical factors leading to these decisions and their implications for interpreting sepsis mortality are not well characterized. Methods We performed a secondary analysis of a prospective observational cohort of adults with physician adjudicated sepsis at a tertiary academic medical center. Patients who transitioned to comfort measures only (CMO) during the index hospitalization underwent structured chart review to characterize baseline health and functional status, clinical severity, care preferences, anticipated outcomes following survival, and the primary reason for CMO transition. Results Among 239 patients with adjudicated sepsis, 42 (17.6%) transitioned to CMO. These patients had substantial underlying disease, including malignancy in 76% and immunocompromised status in 62%. papers.title: Multimorbidity in tuberculosis and its impact on health and treatment outcomes: A prospective cohort study
papers.summary: Multimorbidity - the co-existence of two or more long-term health conditions (LTCs) - is increasingly common in low- and middle-income countries. Yet, in the African region, its prevalence in people with tuberculosis (TB) and its impact on treatment outcomes remain poorly characterised. We sought to determine the prevalence and patterns of multimorbidity and its impact on health and treatment outcomes in people with TB in Kampala, Uganda, and to evaluate cascades of care for hypertension, diabetes mellitus, HIV and mental health conditions. This was a prospective cohort study of adults ([≥]18 years) commencing anti-TB treatment at four clinics in Kampala between June 2024-June 2025. LTCs were identified through self-report, validated screening tools, clinical examination and blood analysis, using definitions informed by the Ho et al. Delphi consensus. Multimorbidity was defined as TB plus two or more LTCs. Participants were followed to month six to assess health-related quality of l

papers.title: Diagnostic accuracy of anti-HlyE and LPS antibodies in typhoid intestinal perforation in Niger
papers.summary: Typhoid intestinal perforation (TIP) is a late complication of Salmonella enterica serovar Typhi infection, and blood cultures, if available, are often negative at this stage, making etiologic confirmation challenging. In areas without access to blood culture diagnostics, TIP incidence can serve as a proxy for enteric fever burden. Antibodies against hemolysin E (HlyE) and S. Typhi lipopolysaccharide (LPS) are promising serologic markers for typhoid, but their diagnostic utility for TIP remains unclear. In this study, we assessed the diagnostic accuracy of anti-HlyE and anti-LPS IgG and IgA antibodies measured by kinetic enzyme immunoassay in children undergoing emergency laparotomy for acute abdomen in Niger. Dried blood spots (DBS) were collected pre-operatively (baseline) and within 30 days post-hospital discharge (convalescence). papers.title: Validation of an electronic-nose sensor array in detecting C. difficile and differentiating toxin-positive from toxin-negative stool samples
papers.summary: Objective: To evaluate the specimen-level performance of a multichannel electronic nose (e-nose) sensor array in classifying stool specimens into relevant Clostridioides difficile categories. Design: Retrospective single-center validation study with reference to polymerase chain reaction (PCR) and C. difficile toxin testing. Participants: A convenience sample of 31 discarded stool specimens with PCR and confirmatory toxin testing. Categorized into PCR-positive (+)/toxin+, PCR+/toxin-negative (-), and PCR-. Methods: Specimens were sampled in controlled headspace by two e-nose sensor arrays in 10-minute sessions with 5-second sampling intervals. The primary endpoint was one-versus rest classification performance (sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, and accuracy) into three classes: PCR+/toxin+, PCR+/toxin-, and PCR-. papers.title: Increased sensitivity of detecting variation in malaria endemicity by parasite density measurement in large surveys
papers.summary: Introduction: The continuing high and inequitable global malaria burden requires improved methods to understand trends and target control. Current methods often involve infection prevalence surveys, but additional parasitological measures could increase precision in estimating infection burdens of communities. Methods: Focusing on the country with most malaria globally, examinations of slides from 10,651 children under five sampled in the 2021 national Malaria Indicator Survey in Nigeria were performed to measure asexual parasite densities in infected children and discriminate sexual stages and species. Variation in these indices among the six different geopolitical zones and 37 individual states including the Federal Capital Territory were compared with the variation indicated by infection prevalence alone. papers.title: Evaluating Behavioral Parallelism and Cost Incentives in Voluntary Quarantine: A Randomized App-Based Epidemic Game at VinUniversity in Hanoi, Vietnam
papers.summary: Background: Quantifying behavioral drivers of protective action during infectious disease outbreaks remains challenging. App-based experimental epidemic games (epigames) provide a framework for studying these decisions in naturalistic settings, but correspondence between in-game measures and real-life beliefs or behaviors requires evaluation. We examined whether an activity-based opportunity cost influenced voluntary quarantine decisions within an epigame and whether real-life health beliefs transferred into the game and predicted observed choices. Methods: We conducted a two-week randomized controlled trial from May 4 to May 17, 2026, at VinUniversity (VinUni) in Hanoi, Vietnam. Participants using the Epigames app installed in their smartphone were randomized to a low-barrier group, earning 1 point per qualifying contact with other participant when remaining active, or a high-barrier group, earning 2 points per contact. papers.title: Data Reduction in SARS-CoV-2 Amplicon Sequencing: Effects of Read Subsampling and Normalization on Consensus Quality, Lineage Assignment, and Computational Burden
papers.summary: BackgroundAmplicon-based next-generation sequencing is a cornerstone of viral genomic surveillance, but it often produces datasets with highly uneven read coverage due to PCR amplification bias. This leads to excessive data generation and substantial computational overhead for downstream bioinformatic analysis. ResultsWe evaluated the efficacy of two data reduction strategies on 220 SARS-CoV-2 clinical specimens and 12 wastewater samples: random subsampling with SeqKit and read depth normalization with BBNorm. FASTQ files were reduced to target depths from 10X to 10,000X to compare genome coverage, lineage assignment concordance, and computational resource usage. papers.title: Does gut microbial richness lost with industrialisation matter for infection? A two-direction test in Gambian toddlers
papers.summary: Background and objectives: Industrialisation is associated with lower gut microbial richness. The ecological insurance hypothesis proposes that richer communities buffer disturbance via overlapping functions, possibly affecting infection susceptibility. We state predictions, audit the evidence, and test the richness-infection relationship in Gambian children. Methodology: We analysed 452 children aged 6-35 months with Day 85 stool 16S profiles and dated infections over 113 days. Diversity used Hill numbers (q = 0, 1, 2); redundancy was inferred from reference-genome gene content. We examined associations with illness during follow-up and infections after Day 85, adjusting for earlier illness. papers.title: Longitudinal Multi-omics Reveals Persistent Gut Microbial and Metabolic Dysbiosis Following Anti-Tuberculosis Therapy
papers.summary: Pulmonary tuberculosis (TB) is associated with systemic alterations extending beyond the lungs, yet the longitudinal impact of anti-tuberculosis therapy (ATT) on gut ecosystem recovery remains poorly understood. Here, we performed a longitudinal multi-omics analysis of gut microbial and metabolic dynamics in pulmonary TB patients (n=8) followed at baseline, 1, 6, and 8 months of ATT, compared with healthy household contacts (HHCs; n=8). Shotgun metagenomics, functional profiling, untargeted fecal metabolomics, resistome, plasmidome, virome, and microbiome-metabolome integration analyses were performed to characterize disease-associated alterations and treatment-associated recovery. Active, treatment-naive TB was characterized by reduced microbial diversity, altered community structure, depletion of beneficial commensals, and disruption of microbial functional pathways and metabolic profiles. papers.title: Hepatitis E Virus Prevalence and Associated Risk Factors in Pregnant Women Attending Antenatal Consultations Niger Republic, 2025
papers.summary: BackgroundHepatitis E virus (HEV) is highly endemic in several African countries with high mortality rate among pregnant women. The prevalence of HEV in Niger among pregnant women is unknown. We hereby aim to report the prevalence and risk factors of HEV among pregnant women in Niamey, Niger. MethodsBlood samples were collected from pregnant women attending antenatal consultation in three selected Health centers in Niamey. Data were collected for socio demographic characteristics using a structured questionnaire. Samples were tested using ELISA and qRT-PCR for anti-HEV IgM and RNA detection respectively. HEV associated risk factors were determined using multivariate logistic regression models. ResultsA total of 491 pregnant women were enrolled with mean age of 26.5 years. papers.title: Effects of XFG-adapted mRNA vaccination on SARS-CoV-2 variant neutralisation
papers.summary: SARS-CoV-2 antigenic evolution continues to challenge strain-matched vaccination. papers.title: Absolute and Relative Effectiveness of High-Dose vs Standard-Dose Influenza Vaccines Against Severe Outcomes in Older Adults
papers.summary: ImportanceSeveral influenza vaccine products are available for older adults, but evidence combining both their absolute effectiveness and head-to-head comparisons within the same large population remains scarce, limiting product-specific vaccination guidance for this high-risk group. ObjectiveTo estimate the relative and absolute effectiveness of influenza vaccines against influenza- related hospitalization and in-hospital mortality among older adults. Design, Setting, and ParticipantsNationwide cohort study using the French National Health Data System (SNDS), including all adults born in 1958 or earlier, living in metropolitan France, at the start of the 2023-2024 campaign. Relative effectiveness (rVE) was assessed using a landmark design with exposure fixed before epidemic onset. Absolute effectiveness (VE) was assessed using a sequential trial emulation with weekly matching of newly vaccinated individuals to yet unvaccinated controls. papers.title: Quantifying the current and future risk of West Nile virus and Usutu virus in humans and horses across England and Wales using an R0-based suitability metric
papers.summary: In England and Wales, Usutu virus (USUV) was detected in 2020 and is now established. West Nile virus (WNV) has so far only been detected in a single location, in two Aedes vexans mosquito pools sampled during 2023 surveillance. Given the growing threat to the UK from Culex-borne viruses there is a need to undertake risk assessments to contribute to preparedness and surveillance strategy for both viruses across human and animal health sectors. Here, we present the first application of a mechanistic R-based model, incorporating temperature dependence and combining data on vector species distribution with projected future climate scenarios, to assess transmission suitability for WNV and USUV across England and Wales. papers.title: Model-guided placement of decentralized diagnostics for spatial control of the 2026 Bundibugyo Ebola epidemic
papers.summary: Before 2026, Bundibugyo virus disease had only two recognized outbreaks. By August 2026, delayed recognition and multi-day sample transport in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo had contributed to a large, spatially dispersed epidemic. We hypothesized that model-guided placement of decentralized diagnostics in frontier health zones could help contain spatial spread by acting as a spatial fence: delayed recognition would be converted into timely polymerase chain reaction (PCR) confirmation, isolation, and contact tracing before imported lineages became established. papers.title: Measuring enteric pathogen force of infection through antibody responses in children
papers.summary: Enteric pathogens account for a substantial global disease burden, yet population-based surveillance remains limited by the transient nature of pathogen shedding, which constrains the sensitivity of stool-based molecular testing to a narrow detection window. Detection of IgG responses in serological surveys could enable new insights into enteric pathogen transmission, but benchmarking serological measures relative to stool-based measures of infection remains a critical evidence gap. papers.title: The Health and Economic Impact of the Adult-specific 21-valent (aPCV21) Pneumococcal Conjugate Vaccine vs PCV20 on Invasive Pneumococcal Disease Among Adults Aged 65 years in the United Kingdom: A Modeling Study
papers.summary: IntroductionThis study compared the health and economic impact of the 21-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine (aPCV21) vs the 20-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine (PCV20) on invasive pneumococcal disease (IPD) and post-meningitis sequelae (PMS) among adults aged 65 years and older in the United Kingdom (UK). MethodsA published Markov model was used to simulate a single-cohort of vaccine-naive adults who became eligible for age-based vaccination at age 65 years, with uptake occurring over time. The cohort was followed until a maximum age of 100 years. Model inputs were derived from publicly available national health data and published reports. Outcomes were discounted at 3.5% annually, and costs were adjusted to the 2024 Great Britain Pound ({pound}). Additional analyses explored the impact of changing the age-based recommendation from 65 years to 75 years. papers.title: Not Sick, Yet Treated: Barriers and Facilitators to Tuberculosis Preventive Treatment Uptake Among Household Contacts of Tuberculosis Patients in Moulvibazar District, Bangladesh
papers.summary: IntroductionPreventing tuberculosis (TB) through TB Preventive Treatment (TPT) is an essential component of TB control and elimination. In recent years, many countries including Bangladesh, have revised their national programs to extend TPT to household contacts of TB patients. However, coverage remains well below the target, and evidence remains limited on context-specific barriers and facilitators. This study aimed to explore the barriers and facilitators to TPT uptake among household contacts in Bangladesh. MethodsThis study followed an exploratory qualitative approach. The setting was Moulvibazar district, Bangladesh. Qualitative data were collected through key-informant interviews with health providers and in-depth interviews with household contacts, and participants were selected through purposive sampling. papers.title: Metabolic Signatures of Resistance to Mycobacterium Tuberculosis Infection: Insights from a Multi-Country Plasma Metabolomics Study
papers.summary: BackgroundTuberculosis (TB) remains the leading infectious disease cause of mortality worldwide. A subset of individuals exposed to Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) remain TST/IGRA-negative despite sustained exposure, termed "TB resisters". The biological mechanisms underlying this resistance remain poorly understood. We applied untargeted high-resolution metabolomics to determine whether systemic metabolic profiles differ between TB resisters and matched Mtb-infected close contacts. MethodsWe compared untargeted high-resolution plasma metabolomics using liquid chromatography mass spectrometry between 269 TB resisters and 269 matched Mtb-infected close contacts, enrolled across Brazil, India, and South Africa. TB resisters were defined as highly exposed close contacts who slept in the same room or spent at least 5 hours indoors per day with an infectious pulmonary TB index patient, but remained TST/IGRA-negative. papers.title: Can large language models extract travel history from clinical text? A multi-annotator benchmark study
papers.summary: International travel can increase infection risk and spread antimicrobial resistance (AMR), yet clinical systems rarely capture travel history in a structured format. Extracting this information from free-text clinical documentation at scale could improve alerts for high-consequence infections and AMR surveillance. We developed an annotation framework covering key aspects of travel history, including destination, exposures, travel duration, and multiple temporal variables. papers.summary: There is currently no clinical data for the effectiveness of the only licensed Ebola virus disease vaccine (Ervebo) against Bundibugyo virus disease. A number of studies have shown immune cross-reactivity with Bundibugyo virus after Ervebo vaccination. However, antibody recognition of Bundibugyo is around 2.8-fold lower than recognition of Ebola virus. Here, we aimed to infer how a 2.8-fold drop in immune recognition may affect Ervebo protection against Bundibugyo virus disease based on analysis of data on Ervebo immunogenicity and protection from Ebola virus disease. This work has three main components. Firstly, we analysed the timing of vaccine protection in the Ervebo pivotal ring vaccination clinical trial. papers.summary: Urogenital schistosomiasis, caused by Schistosoma haematobium, remains a major public health challenge among school-aged children in rural Ghana. Although urogenital indicators are well- established, systemic hepatic biomarker alterations in post-mass drug administration pediatric settings remain poorly characterized. This cross-sectional study evaluated point-of-care urinalysis profiles alongside a panel of serum hepatic and renal biomarkers in 174 children (aged 3-16 years) from the Sene West District, Ghana. Active infection (urine microscopy egg detection) was identified in 84 participants (48.3%, median egg count = 4.50 eggs/10 mL, IQR: 1.00-9.25). Active infection was strongly associated with microhematuria (57.1% vs. 11.1%, p < 0.001), proteinuria (42.9% vs. 22.2%, p = 0.004), and leukocyturia (27.4% vs. 4.4%, p < 0.001). papers.title: Real-time situational assessment of respiratory virus epidemics in Australia over winter 2025 and an out-of-season influenza A H3N2 epidemic
papers.summary: IntroductionIn temperate regions, influenza and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) typically exhibit seasonal epidemics during the winter months, often concurrently with SARS-CoV-2 epidemics. Monitoring past and real-time trends in infection dynamics is important for informing public health situational awareness, including identifying and characterising unusual epidemic activity. However, data used to monitor these trends can exhibit substantial noise including strong day-of-the-week variation in reporting. In addition, case data for influenza can obscure distinct trends in influenza subtypes if not combined with virological data. papers.title: Parametric Models for Predicting Gram-negative Antibiotic Susceptibility Phenotype: A Brief Report
papers.summary: Predicted probabilities of antibiotic susceptibility to known or suspected pathogens can be used to support antibiotic selection. Patient demographic, clinical, and prior microbiologic history can be used to generate location-specific prediction models. For three Canadian tertiary care institutions we fit and evaluated models for predicting Gram-negative antibiotic susceptibilities to common antimicrobial agents based on previously established model structures. A web-based application was developed to permit visualization of antibiotic susceptibility predictions and support antibiotic decision-making.

papers.title: VSV-EBOV vaccination induces cross-reactive T-cell responses against Bundibugyo virus in humans
papers.summary: Bundibugyo ebolavirus (BDBV) is causing an ongoing outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) with no licensed vaccine available. Recent reports have shown the presence of BDBV-cross-reactive antibody responses in humans vaccinated against the related Ebola virus (EBOV). Here, we used an IFN-{gamma} ELISpot assay to assess T cell responses against the EBOV, BDBV and SUDV glycoproteins in clinical trial participants vaccinated with the licensed VSV-EBOV vaccine. We could show that BDBV-cross-reactive T cell responses are detectable in the majority of individuals and that conserved regions within the glycoprotein are targeted. In the absence of a BDBV-specific vaccine, these data support efficacy trials of the VSV-EBOV vaccine during the current outbreak.

papers.summary: In medical practice, the rising prevalence of infections in kidney transplant recipients (KTRs) is a notable concern. papers.title: Next-generation immune cell engagers for B cell depletion in autoimmune diseases
papers.summary: Nature Reviews Drug Discovery, Published online: 07 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41573-026-01534-z Immune cell engagers are emerging as a strategy for deep B cell depletion in autoimmune diseases. This Review examines their mechanisms, clinical development and next-generation designs, including T cell, natural killer cell and γδ T cell-engaging formats, and considers lessons from haematological malignancies to improve efficacy, safety and durability of immune modulation.

papers.title: COPD trial wins spur broad respiratory hopes
papers.summary: Nature Reviews Drug Discovery, Published online: 05 October 2026; doi:10.1038/d41573-026-00162-x AstraZeneca’s tozorakimab reduced disease flare ups in patients with COPD, suggesting IL-33-targeted antibodies could offer broad potential in pulmonary diseases.

papers.title: Soft drugs: design principles and topical applications
papers.summary: Nature Reviews Drug Discovery, Published online: 30 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41573-026-01535-y Soft drugs are designed to enhance drug safety, undergoing rapid and predictable metabolic inactivation after exerting their therapeutic effect. This review provides an overview of the principles of soft drug design, highlighting examples of topical soft drugs in development, practical considerations, ongoing challenges and future directions.

papers.title: Psychedelic protects against chemotherapy-induced nerve damage

papers.title: The cellular landscape of druggable RNA-binding proteins
papers.summary: Nature Reviews Drug Discovery, Published online: 29 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41573-026-01531-2 RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) regulate every step of cellular RNA metabolism, and their dysregulation contributes to many diseases. This Perspective describes the endogenous and disease-linked roles of RBPs and strategies for their therapeutic targeting, including opportunities that arise from the recent discovery of RBPs localized to the cell surface.

papers.title: Metastasizing cancer cells leave an immunogenic trail
papers.summary: Nature Reviews Immunology, Published online: 09 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41577-026-01366-3 Metastasizing cancer cells release migrasomes containing tumour-specific antigens that can promote T cell responses.

papers.title: LAG3 checkpoint function and its mechanism of action in therapeutic targeting
papers.summary: Nature Reviews Immunology, Published online: 09 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41577-026-01359-2 This Review explores how the immune checkpoint receptor lymphocyte activation gene 3 (LAG3) suppresses T cell activity through newly defined signalling mechanisms, including tonic and ligand-induced pathways. The Review highlights therapeutic advances, biomarker strategies and emerging opportunities to target LAG3 in cancer and autoimmune disease.

papers.title: A guide to B cell metabolism
papers.summary: Nature Reviews Immunology, Published online: 07 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41577-026-01355-6 Metabolic control is an integral component of B cell physiology, shaping fate decisions and effector functions, while also driving maladaptive programmes that contribute to diverse pathologies. This Review provides an overview of the current understanding of B cell metabolism in health and disease.

papers.title: Sympathetic nerve activity primes susceptibility to autoimmune hair loss
papers.summary: Nature Reviews Immunology, Published online: 05 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41577-026-01365-4 A study in Nature by Cui et al. reports that sympathetic nerve activity during the growth phase of hair follicles activates endogenous retroviruses, leading to an innate immune response that destabilizes immune privilege.

papers.title: The effects of IFNγ on tissue physiology through structural cells
papers.summary: Nature Reviews Immunology, Published online: 29 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41577-026-01357-4 In this Perspective, the authors use examples from evolution, animal models of disease and clinical results to explore how IFNγ, a quintessential antipathogen cytokine, also has a fundamental role in tissue homeostasis and organ function through its effects on non-haematopoietic structural cells.

papers.title: Drugging the immune system: principles of immunopharmacology
papers.summary: Nature Reviews Immunology, Published online: 28 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41577-026-01361-8 Immune-based therapies have transformed the treatment of cancer and inflammatory and autoimmune diseases, but treatment is often suboptimal and the ability to predictably harness the immune system for new therapies remains limited. The pharmacology of immune-based drugs may be distinct from that of many traditional therapies. Here, I outline four principles of ‘immunopharmacology’ that provide a framework for understanding how the immune system responds to therapeutic perturbation. These principles may help to better define how immune-based therapies work and identify new opportunities for drugging the immune system.

papers.title: ‘Trained’ sensory neurons drive allergic sensitization
papers.summary: Nature Reviews Immunology, Published online: 28 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41577-026-01362-7 A study in Immunity reports that protease allergens ‘train’ sensory neurons through metabolic remodelling to enhance the response to re-exposure.

papers.title: What the ‘negative space’ tells us about the immunology of multiple sclerosis
papers.summary: Nature Reviews Immunology, Published online: 28 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41577-026-01358-3 By exploring five enduring “negative spaces” in multiple sclerosis (MS) research, Kaufmann, Gold and Fugger challenge simple explanations of disease pathogenesis. Their Comment argues that MS emerges from complex interactions between immunity, infection and tissue resilience, offering a fresh framework for understanding progression and therapeutic intervention.

papers.title: The role of the respiratory microbiome in acute and chronic respiratory diseases
papers.summary: Nature Reviews Microbiology, Published online: 09 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41579-026-01377-w In this Review, Heinzinger, Segal and Dickson summarize recent advances in our understanding of the respiratory microbiome in health, examine how it is altered in acute and chronic respiratory diseases, and discuss its diagnostic and therapeutic potential.

papers.title: Remediation restores soil carbon
papers.summary: Nature Reviews Microbiology, Published online: 07 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41579-026-01384-x This study suggests that shifts in bioavailable heavy metals during soil remediation reshape microbial physiological traits, thereby increasing microbial carbon use efficiency and enhancing soil carbon storage.

papers.title: Towards broader-spectrum direct-acting antivirals against RNA viruses
papers.summary: Nature Reviews Microbiology, Published online: 07 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41579-026-01372-1 In this Review, Neyts and colleagues discuss the rationale for developing broader-spectrum antivirals against RNA viruses, survey promising antiviral targets and agents, and outline strategies to accelerate clinical development and strengthen outbreak preparedness.

papers.title: Predicting resistance evolution to guide antibiotic development
papers.summary: Nature Reviews Microbiology, Published online: 07 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41579-026-01373-0 Resistance emergence is a major challenge to antibiotic development, often undermining promising drug candidates and negating years of research and pharmaceutical investment. In this Review, Pál and colleagues propose a resistance-based classification system for antibiotic development that integrates early resistance predictions into the prospective development of new antibiotics.

papers.title: Cities cannot go green without soil microorganisms
papers.summary: Nature Reviews Microbiology, Published online: 02 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41579-026-01380-1 Urban soils must move from providing single, engineered functions to supporting multifunctionality. Managing their microbiomes could simultaneously strengthen climate regulation, water retention, pollutant removal, biodiversity and human health, but only if biological restoration is coupled to risk assessment, long-term monitoring and equitable access.

papers.title: How bacterial immune systems sense phage infection
papers.summary: Nature Reviews Microbiology, Published online: 02 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41579-026-01376-x Bacteria deploy diverse immune systems to counter phage infection, yet how these systems sense invasion remains incompletely understood. This Review categorizes phage-derived triggers and outlines emerging principles that govern immune recognition of phage infection.

papers.title: Microbial ecology of shallow groundwater ecosystems
papers.summary: Nature Reviews Microbiology, Published online: 01 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41579-026-01362-3 In this Review, Karwautz and Griebler examine the microbial communities found in shallow groundwater and aquifers, exploring their diversity, functional roles and dynamic interactions with adjacent terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems, as well as the influence of global change and anthropogenic pressures on these microorganisms.

papers.title: Microbial synthesis and degradation of bio-based biodegradable plastics
papers.summary: Nature Reviews Microbiology, Published online: 01 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41579-026-01370-3 In this Review, O’Connor and colleagues discuss the contributions of microorganisms across the life cycle of key bio-based polymers and assess the current role, the potential and limitations of microbial production and degradation of bio-based polymers as well as the implications for integration of microbiological processes into a circular bioeconomy.

papers.summary: Science Immunology, Volume 11, Issue 124 , October 2026.

papers.summary: Science Immunology, Volume 11, Issue 124 , October 2026.

papers.summary: Science Immunology, Volume 11, Issue 124 , October 2026.

papers.summary: Science Immunology, Volume 11, Issue 124 , October 2026.

papers.title: Spatially tuned localization of interleukins and OX40 agonists enhances synergistic anti-tumor immunity
papers.summary: Klich et al. use a hydrogel to deliver immunotherapy combinations intratumorally and peritumorally. Rational selection of the site of administration drives tumor clearance and long-term survivors.

papers.title: Breastfeeding and maternal microbial reservoirs are associated with infant gut phageome development during the first year of life
papers.summary: Cabello-Yeves et al. use longitudinal metagenomic analysis of mother-infant dyads to show that infant gut phageomes diversify during the first year of life and are associated with feeding-related variables and maternal microbial reservoirs. Persistent bifidophages dominate early communities, highlighting the potential relevance of phages in microbiome-targeted early-life interventions.

papers.title: Anti-HDGFL2 cryptic protein antibodies provide a sensitive readout of TDP-43 pathology and clinical disease features
papers.summary: Citrano, Maheswari Jawahar et al. develop sensitive immunoassays using second-generation polyclonal and monoclonal antibodies against HDGFL2-CE proteins and show that their levels in brain tissue associate with pTDP-43 pathology, earlier symptom onset, and shorter survival in patients with FTLD-TDP and FTLD-TDP/MND.

papers.title: AI-integrated RNA therapeutics in precision oncology
papers.summary: Symmans et al. review how artificial intelligence supports RNA therapeutic development in precision oncology, spanning multi-omics target prioritization and RNA design to delivery, patient stratification, manufacturing, and clinical translation. They distinguish clinically supported applications from preclinical and speculative approaches, outlining validation, governance, and regulatory requirements.

papers.title: Microbiota-regulated TCDCA associates with Parkinson’s disease severity and promotes BBB dysfunction through VSMC TGR5 signaling in mice
papers.summary: Zhao et al. show that circulating TCDCA associates with Parkinson’s disease severity and that TCDCA administration worsens neurovascular and motor outcomes in mice. VSMC TGR5 deletion and BSH-active L. reuteri interventions implicate a microbiota-regulated TCDCA-BBB pathway while defining its translational limitations.

papers.title: Reviving low-affinity glycan-targeting CAR with combinatorial design
papers.summary: Forcados et al. develop and test a combinatorial CAR strategy against B cell lymphoma, in which they combine CD75s and CD19 targeting. This combinatorial approach overcomes the limited efficiency of CD75s mono-targeting and lowers the risk of CAR-related toxicity seen with CD19 single targeting.

papers.title: Human genetic evidence challenges NCOA1 as a monogenic obesity gene
papers.summary: Delplanque et al. combine large-scale human genetics with functional analyses to reassess the role of NCOA1 in obesity. Despite its biological plausibility within the melanocortin pathway, pathogenic NCOA1 variants were not associated with adiposity, questioning their relevance for precision obesity therapies targeting this pathway.

papers.title: Prognostic value of cfDNA methylation in locally advanced esophageal squamous cell cancer treated with neoadjuvant immunochemoradiotherapy
papers.summary: Chen et al. track cfDNA methylation during neoadjuvant immunochemoradiotherapy for esophageal squamous cell carcinoma. Methylation signals decline with treatment and are associated with pathological response and disease-free survival. The decline is reproduced in a separate 30-patient cohort, supporting further evaluation of cfDNA methylation for noninvasive monitoring.

papers.title: Microbiota-mediated naringenin release limits postoperative acute gastrointestinal injury by suppressing ferroptosis
papers.summary: Deng et al. show that reduced preoperative fecal naringenin and β-glucuronidase activity associate with postoperative acute gastrointestinal injury after cardiopulmonary bypass. Mechanistically, microbial β-glucuronidase promotes naringenin release and limits epithelial ferroptosis, highlighting candidate noninvasive biomarkers and a potential microbiota-based intervention axis.

papers.title: A spatiotemporal atlas of radiation-induced brain injury reveals dysfunction of the blood-CSF barrier
papers.summary: Quan et al. construct a spatiotemporal transcriptomic atlas of radiation-induced brain injury and show that loss of radiosensitive Tmsb4x+ choroid plexus epithelial cells triggers blood-CSF barrier dysfunction and macrophage infiltration that sustains interferon-responsive microglial activation. These findings position the blood-CSF barrier as a potential target for mitigating post-irradiation neuroinflammation.

papers.title: Lipid-engineered antibody-based therapeutics target inflamed joints and lymph nodes to enhance rheumatoid arthritis treatment
papers.summary: Zhao et al. attach multiple lipid motifs to antibody-based biologic disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drugs (bDMARDs), enabling them to engage multiple albumin molecules in vivo and enhancing their accumulation in inflamed joints and lymph nodes. This generalizable strategy can target therapeutics larger than albumin to inflammatory sites for improved rheumatoid arthritis treatment.

papers.title: Regional brain aging signatures predict mortality through neurovascular immune mechanisms
papers.summary: Lee et al. integrate structural brain MRI with plasma proteomics to identify a three-region brain age model that predicts mortality more accurately than global measures and reveals shared immune and vascular mechanisms. These findings support regional brain aging as a scalable biomarker for precision geromedicine.

papers.title: A standardized patient-derived glioblastoma organoid platform for evaluating radiotherapy efficacy and overcoming resistance
papers.summary: Wang et al. develop a standardized reaggregated glioblastoma organoid (rGBO) platform that enables scalable evaluation of patient-specific treatment responses. The platform links organoid radiosensitivity with patient survival, identifies response-related transcriptomic signatures, and reveals BET inhibition as a strategy to enhance radiotherapy efficacy in organoid and xenograft models.

papers.title: A translational pipeline for classification of variants of uncertain significance to support gene therapy clinical trial in OTOF-related deafness
papers.summary: Chen et al. establish a translational functional pipeline to reclassify OTOF variants of uncertain significance. This pipeline enables definitive molecular diagnosis and eligibility for gene therapy trials; it further reveals that K1992R drives pathogenicity in the E1700Q haplotype via disrupting otoferlin localization.

papers.title: Oral microbial nitrate metabolism is associated with lower prevalence of prediabetes
papers.summary: Zhao et al. investigate the role of the tongue microbiome in prediabetes and glycemic dysregulation. Rothia mucilaginosa and microbial nitrate metabolism are associated with lower prediabetes prevalence and improve the prediction of prediabetes progression, highlighting oral nitrate metabolism as a potential modifiable link between the oral microbiome and metabolic health.

papers.title: Fusion-loop-engineered Zika mRNA vaccine elicits convergent B cell immunodominance to uncouple protection from ADE in macaques
papers.summary: Yang et al. demonstrate, in primates, that a fusion-loop-engineered Zika mRNA vaccine confers full protection with negligible dengue ADE. The response is dominated by convergent B cells orthologous to human IGHV5-10-1 whose antibodies target a distinct viral hotspot, with DENV envelope N67-linked glycan preventing cross-reactivity for safer flavivirus vaccines.

papers.title: Disruption of the Nav1.8/Ankyrin-3 interaction in nociceptors reduces pathological pain-like behaviors in mice
papers.summary: Chronic pain is a complex neurobiological problem whose solution is elusive. Powell et al. describe an approach to reduce chronic neuropathic pain in rodent models using a short lipidated peptide designed to inhibit the interaction between Nav1.8 and Ankyrin-3.

papers.title: Bridging innate and adaptive immunity: A bispecific SIRPαD1-αPCSK9 fusion protein reprograms macrophages for durable tumor clearance
papers.summary: Xu et al. show that blocking the CD47-SIRPα phagocytic checkpoint paradoxically elevates tumor-derived PCSK9, which degrades MHC-I on macrophages and impairs antigen cross-presentation to CD8+ T cells. A bispecific fusion protein co-targeting CD47 and PCSK9 overcomes this resistance, restoring T cell priming and achieving tumor control with improved safety.

papers.title: From patient cells to patient therapy: Twenty years of iPSC-based translation in neurodegenerative disease
papers.summary: Cha and Kim review two decades of iPSC-based translation in neurodegenerative disease, highlighting disease-specific therapeutic logic and the emerging importance of transplantation biology. They propose a phase-resolved framework for the post-transplant “biological black box” linking graft survival, maturation, host interactions, and long-term therapeutic outcome.

papers.title: Multi-omics-driven personalized management of advanced HCC
papers.summary: Sheng et al. integrate spatial multi-omics, functional models, and clinical validation to show that fibrotic stroma suppresses epithelial cGAS-STING signaling and T cell recruitment in HCC. Their GCSS model links tumor architecture to response prediction for TACE plus immune checkpoint blockade.

papers.title: Enhanced liver regeneration via targeted mRNA delivery for partial in vivo reprogramming
papers.summary: Jo et al. show that transient OSKM induction generates two distinct liver progenitor-like cell populations with limited immune activation. Liver-targeted OSKM mRNA-LNPs induce hepatocyte dedifferentiation and enhance regeneration after acetaminophen-induced liver injury, supporting transient hepatic reprogramming as a strategy for inducing regenerative plasticity with therapeutic potential for acute injury.

papers.title: In vivo-edited CCR7+IL-7+ DCs reverse T cell exhaustion by promoting T memory stem cell differentiation
papers.summary: Fu and Ma et al. develop DVH to edit DCs into CCR7+IL-7+ DCs, which target the T-zone within TDLNs and secrete IL-7 to promote Tscm differentiation. The Tscms can self-renew and generate effector T cells under antigen stimulation continuously, thereby killing tumor cells and reducing T cell exhaustion at the source.

papers.title: EZH2-dependent phenotypic plasticity reveals TTP-associated and mTORC1 therapeutic vulnerabilities in lethal prostate cancer
papers.summary: German et al. use integrated multi-omics analysis to identify EZH2 as a central regulator of prostate cancer phenotypic plasticity. The study reveals TTP-associated pathways and adaptive PI3K/mTORC1 as mediators of response to EZH2 inhibition and demonstrates that co-targeting EZH2 and PI3K/mTORC1 is an effective strategy in aggressive prostate cancer models.

papers.title: Reversal of the neutrophil barrier for potentiating immune-engineered bacteria therapy in pancreatic cancer
papers.summary: Guan et al. develop an IAA-assisted engineered bacterial therapy for pancreatic cancer. IAA suppresses neutrophil recruitment and synergizes with gemcitabine to eliminate neutrophils, boosting bacterial colonization and antitumor immune efficacy.

papers.title: A multi-omics analysis of advanced triple-negative breast cancer identifies predictors to chemo-immunotherapy and on-treatment dynamics
papers.summary: Van Renne, Agostinetto, et al. perform a multi-omics characterization of advanced TNBC to identify response predictors and treatment-induced dynamics during chemo-ICI. Poor outcomes are associated with fibrovascular and myeloid remodeling, highlighting coordinated resistance mechanisms, actionable therapeutic targets, and the value of microenvironment-based stratification for future ICI-based trials.

papers.title: Potently neutralizing and protective human monoclonal antibodies against the measles fusion protein trimer
papers.summary: Handal et al. isolate a panel of naturally occurring human monoclonal antibodies against the measles fusion protein that potently neutralize in vitro and inhibit viral replication in vivo, demonstrating strong clinical potential. Two antibodies bind distinct portions of the F protein simultaneously with epitopes spanning across multiple F protomers.

papers.title: Structural basis for broad orthopoxvirus neutralization by two antibodies targeting distinct L1R epitopes
papers.summary: Chen et al. identify two neutralizing antibodies, G4 and B9, targeting distinct epitopes on the mpox virus M1R protein (an L1R homolog). Despite targeting a conventional epitope, G4 overcomes Asp35-associated neutralization escape. Both antibodies protect against multiple orthopoxviruses in vitro and in vivo, supporting their potential as broad-spectrum antiviral candidates.

papers.title: Potentiating immunotherapy in “immune-cold” solid tumors through orchestrating T cell immunity via tumor-specific genetic engineering
papers.summary: (Cell Reports Medicine 6, 102510; December 16, 2025)

papers.title: Human iPSC models of myocardial infarction: From injury to repair and therapeutic discovery
papers.summary: Johnson et al. review how human induced pluripotent stem cells can model key stages of myocardial infarction, focusing on cell types involved across acute injury, repair, and remodeling. They examine current model strengths and limitations and discuss emerging applications in therapeutic discovery, patient-specific modeling, and regenerative cardiac repair.

papers.title: Punicalin targets RSV glycoprotein and fusion protein at non-overlapping sites to prevent viral escape
papers.summary: Xiong et al. identify that punicalin broadly inhibits respiratory syncytial virus subtypes and clinical isolates by targeting the viral G and F proteins at sites outside known resistance hotspots. It retains potent activity against drug-resistant virus and, when delivered by nebulization, reduces pulmonary viral burden and inflammation in infected mice.

papers.title: Multipronged enhancement of CART cell activity against ROR1 neoantigen by inhibition of H3K27 methyltransferase EZH2
papers.summary: Wang et al. report that inhibition of EZH2 and, to lesser degree, other epigenetic modifiers promotes expression of ROR1 neoantigen on malignant cells. CART cells targeting ROR1 are able to detect the neoantigen at very low concentration and, in combination with EZH2 inhibition, highly effectively eliminate the ROR1-expressing cells.

papers.title: iPSC-derived retinal organoids: Biological insights and progress toward photoreceptor replacement therapy
papers.summary: Mandai et al. review iPSC-derived photoreceptor replacement therapy, contrasting cone precursor and retinal organoid transplantations. They highlight host-dependent cone integration, gene-edited organoids for enhanced integration, and synaptic rewiring in the adult primate retina, providing a framework to restore vision in patients with untreatable retinal degenerations.

papers.title: Functional O-specific polysaccharide-specific antibody responses in young children following Shigella infection in Bangladesh
papers.summary: Bernshtein et al. show that functional antibodies correlate with milder shigellosis at any age, yet only individuals over 5 years of age mount lasting responses to the surface O-specific polysaccharide that drives Shigella uptake by phagocytes and triggers IL-1β and IL-18 release.

papers.title: Genome-wide cell-free DNA methylation profiling via TAPS for moyamoya disease diagnosis and postoperative collateral formation prediction
papers.summary: Chen et al. apply multimodal cell-free DNA (cfDNA) profiling via TET-assisted pyridine borane sequencing to moyamoya disease. They identify cfDNA methylation signatures that distinguish moyamoya disease from atherosclerotic cerebrovascular disease and predict postoperative collateral formation, supporting minimally invasive diagnosis and preoperative assessment of moyamoya disease.

papers.title: Combining pro-resolving therapy with cyclosporine A restores immune homeostasis and reduces toxicity in autoimmune bone marrow failure
papers.summary: Grazda et al. show that defective inflammation resolution persists in autoimmune bone marrow failure, despite standard-of-care cyclosporine A therapy. Combining resolvin E1 with cyclosporine A restores immune homeostasis while reducing toxicity.

papers.title: A blood-based metabolic signature for earlier detection of lung cancer
papers.summary: Irajizad et al. report a blood-based metabolite panel for earlier detection of lung cancer. The metabolite panel complements clinical risk models for lung cancer incidence and mortality. The panel provides a means for identifying ever-smoker individuals at elevated 1-year risk of lung cancer who would benefit from lung cancer screening.

papers.title: Therapeutic oligonucleotides as genetic medicines: The current state and future perspective
papers.summary: Godinho et al. provide an overview of nucleic acid therapies, a new class of programmable drugs that enable disease-modifying treatments by acting at the gene transcript level. The authors summarize key advances in chemistry and delivery and offer a perspective on the advances expected in the near future.

papers.title: Targeting RPL4 improves the therapeutic efficacy of PD-L1 blockade in liver fibrosis
papers.summary: Zhang et al. identify a key profibrotic function of FBXL6 in hepatic stellate cells through activation of the RPL4-YY1-PD-L1-PI3K-AKT-mTOR axis. Targeting RPL4 in combination with PD-L1 blockade achieves near-complete resolution of liver fibrosis.

papers.title: Early diagnosis and molecular classification of gastric cancer peritoneal metastasis by deep learning-driven single-cell lipidomics
papers.summary: Pan et al. combine single-cell lipidomics and graph deep learning to identify occult peritoneal metastasis in gastric cancer. The label-free platform detects rare free cancer cells, supports molecular stratification, and delivers patient-level diagnostic results within 30 min.

papers.title: Characterization of circulating neoantigen-specific T cell responses and public T cell receptors shaping immune memory in Lynch syndrome carriers
papers.summary: Duzagac et al. show that circulating tissue-surveillance neoantigen-specific T cells are detectable in Lynch syndrome carriers, even before cancer onset. Their metabolic states differ by disease stage, separating cancer-free carriers from survivors. Public TCRs spanning blood and tumor tissue open a non-invasive window for immunoprevention in mismatch repair-deficient cancers.

papers.title: Class visualizations and activation atlases for computational pathology
papers.summary: Gustav et al. introduce a concept-level explainability framework that exposes the morphology encoded by a pathology foundation model. The approach reveals prototypical histopathological features and maps the organization and overlap of tissue and cancer concepts, demonstrating that internal model representations reflect both task complexity and pathologist ambiguity.

papers.title: Proteogenomic analysis of pediatric and AYA high-grade glioma reveals age-dependent biology, female-male differences, and kinase targets
papers.summary: Tignor et al. perform a comprehensive proteogenomic analysis of pediatric and AYA high-grade gliomas and identify age- and sex-dependent biology, candidate kinase targets, and proteins and immune signatures associated with poor survival outcomes.

papers.title: Single-cell and spatial multi-omics reveal a recurrent multicellular niche at the tumor-stroma interface in multidrug resistance
papers.summary: Shen et al. map the evolutionary trajectory of multi-drug resistance (MDR) across cancers, revealing a biophysical spatial nexus formed by specific fibroblasts, macrophages, and tumor cells. They demonstrate that dismantling this multicellular barrier-like niche with an FAP/TREM2 bispecific antibody safely restores therapeutic sensitivity, highlighting a targeted strategy to resensitize MDR.

papers.title: Allosteric modulation of YTHDFs by ellagic acid suppresses triple-negative breast cancer via non-canonical activation of the HIF-1α pathway
papers.summary: Zhou et al. identify ellagic acid (EA) as an allosteric inhibitor of YTHDF proteins that binds to a conserved site shared across YTHDF family members. By disrupting YTHDF2-mediated RNA decay, EA stabilizes PFKFB4 mRNA to prevent HIF-1α degradation and upregulates BNIP3 expression, thereby driving triple-negative breast cancer cell death.

papers.title: Single-cell tracking reveals tumor-reactive T cell plasticity during melanoma TIL therapy
papers.summary: Sandholzer et al. track tumor-reactive T cells across TIL therapy in metastatic melanoma using single-cell RNA and TCR sequencing. They show how ex vivo expansion reshapes CD8+ and CD4+ T cell states and links type 17 T cell co-transfer and regulatory T cell expansion to treatment resistance.

papers.title: First-line fecal microbiota transplantation for the management of immune checkpoint inhibitor-mediated diarrhea and colitis
papers.summary: Wang et al. report the efficacy of a preliminary cohort of patients who receive first-line fecal microbiota transplantation for the management of immune-mediated diarrhea and colitis with multi-omics characterization. Response is seen in 10 out of 13 patients, with an increase in alpha-diversity in a majority of patients who respond.

papers.title: Neutrophil elastase-mediated myoepithelial loss is a therapeutic vulnerability in ductal carcinoma in situ progression
papers.summary: Transition from ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) to invasive breast cancer remains a key step in disease progression that is poorly understood. Taifour et al. show that neutrophil elastase disrupts the myoepithelial barrier to promote invasive progression, identifying neutrophil elastase as a potential therapeutic target for high-risk DCIS.

papers.title: Bi-hourly plasma proteomics during the first 48 h of life in an African cohort reveals distinct periods and sex-dependent immune development
papers.summary: Bennike et al. profile plasma proteins and cytokines/chemokines in 679 healthy newborns through mass spectrometry and immunoassays to characterize immune adaptation during the 48 h immediately after birth at bi-hourly resolution. They reveal non-linear trajectories and sex-specific differences especially during day-of-life one, providing a molecular framework for early-life immune development.

papers.title: Targeted insertion of an optimized donor DNA is effective in a humanized mouse model of dominant retinitis pigmentosa
papers.summary: Esposito et al. develop a donor-optimized, mutation-agnostic AAV-HITI strategy for dominant rhodopsin-associated retinitis pigmentosa that simultaneously disrupts the mutant RHO P23H allele and restores rhodopsin expression through targeted integration at the human RHO locus, improving retinal structure, function, and vision in a semi-humanized mouse disease model, up to one year.

papers.title: L013 promotes NRF2 degradation in NRFA-subtype esophageal squamous cell carcinoma
papers.summary: Yu et al. identify L013 as an NRF2-targeting agent that reduces NRF2 via UPS-associated degradation and A51-mediated suppression. L013 inhibits tumor growth in preclinical models, revealing therapeutic potential for NRFA-subtype ESCC.

papers.title: Intoxication and other subjective effects of preanesthetic opioids in surgical patients: A randomized controlled trial
papers.summary: Karlsen et al. show that patients experience marked undesirable effects but minimal desirable effects after preoperative intravenous opioids.

papers.title: Uncovering combination therapies for immune-mediated inflammatory diseases through systems biology analysis on longitudinal patient data
papers.summary: Martínez-Mateu et al. develop a computational framework that uses longitudinal blood transcriptomes from patients with immune-mediated inflammatory diseases to prioritize combination therapies. They identify anti-TNF plus anti-IL-6R as complementary in rheumatoid arthritis, localize the effect to CD14+ monocytes, and validate the combination in mice, nominating candidates for clinical testing.

papers.title: FDA review docs spark Revolution sell-off; Zealand diabetes data underwhelm analysts
papers.summary: The new disclosure suggested Rasonque might not be as broadly effective as previously thought. Elsewhere, Ultragenyx got a much-needed cash infusion and TCGX started a China-focused fund.

papers.title: This week in charts: What’s driving biotech’s recent pullback?
papers.summary: The latest installment in BioPharma Dive’s data visualization series features a look at the factors pressuring biotech stocks of late and the frenetic pace of startup buyouts this year.

papers.title: TRex Bio prices $117M IPO to support immune drug work
papers.summary: Eli Lilly is the largest equity holder in TRex, which is developing drugs that treat immunological conditions by activating “Treg” cells.

papers.title: HHS launches new plan to strengthen vaccine injury research, reporting
papers.summary: Spearheaded by vaccine skeptic Robert F. Kennedy Jr., the initiative will involve a new NIH clinic, an updated monitoring system and reimbursements for doctors who report suspected side effects.

papers.title: Viatris boosts pain drug portfolio with $1.7B buyout of Pacira
papers.summary: The deal hands Viatris two non-opioid pain treatments that booked nearly $700 million in 2025 but could soon lose patent protection. Viatris vowed to use its “intellectual property expertise” to sustain sales.

papers.title: Argenx falls as Sjögren’s setback offsets celiac drug progress
papers.summary: A monitoring board’s recommendation to stop the study for futility took Wall Street by surprise, removing one more ‘blockbuster expansion opportunity’ for Vyvgart.

papers.title: In the hunt for reverse merger targets, Caribou could be prized game
papers.summary: The struggling cell therapy developer is exploring strategic alternatives, which, among other characteristics, make it a likely candidate to receive reverse merger interest.

papers.title: Caribou to halt CAR-T work, lay off staff amid ‘challenging’ funding climate
papers.summary: Despite having an allogeneic cell therapy prospect that’s ready for late-stage testing in lymphoma, Caribou couldn’t secure funding to support the effort and will now pursue “strategic alternatives” instead.

papers.title: Halozyme prevails in patent fight with Merck; Enliven readies anticipated leukemia trial
papers.summary: A Dutch court barred Merck from selling subcutaneous Keytruda in several European countries. Elsewhere, an Insmed executive ended a seven-year run and two startups secured venture cash.

papers.title: A Takeda spinout builds case for its Parkinson’s drug
papers.summary: Cerevance plans to meet with the FDA to determine next steps for a new kind of medicine known as solengepras, now that it has Phase 3 data in hand.
Parkinson’s disease cell therapy-focused Aspen Neuroscience and bispecific biotech Bambusa Therapeutics are the latest drug developers to eye up a public listing.
Becton, Dickinson and Company has named Ferass Abuzaina as its new Worldwide President of its Surgery business unit.
GSK has joined Chai Discovery’s growing roster of Big Pharma clients, signing up to access protein-folding and design models.

As a notorious night owl, it was already very early in the morning of October 5 when Karl Deisseroth, M.D., Ph.D., finally laid down to get some shuteye. Not long after, the phone of the Stanford psychiatrist and bioengineer lit up with an incoming call from Sweden.

As Vir pushes its lead hepatitis D combo through phase 3 development, the biotech has tapped an experienced medical expert to light the way. David Liu, M.D., Ph.D., is now Vir’s chief medical officer, after most recently serving in the same role at Nuvation Bio.
What does it mean to be a Fierce 15 biotech in 2026? With this year’s list unveiled, the Fierce Biotech team gets together to discuss what the winners tell us about the state of the sector.
Eli Lilly-backed TRex Bio and hypertension-focused Retension Pharmaceuticals brought in $116.7 million and $45 million from their respective IPOs, continuing a bumper year for biotech listings.

Endeavor BioMedicines solidified its potential threat to Big Pharma with a phase 2b readout suggesting its Hedgehog inhibitor could become the first drug to reduce lung fibrosis while increasing total lung capacity.
Iambic Therapeutics is aiming to raise $135 million in net proceeds from an IPO as the AI biotech looks to fund the clinical development of its lead cancer drug.
Vacancy rates for lab and manufacturing spaces in Massachusetts increased 11-fold to 31% between 2021 and 2026. So what's gone wrong?
Japan’s Ono Pharmaceutical is paying $80 million upfront for the regional rights to a trio of Biohaven’s IgG degraders, led by a phase 3-stage Grave’s disease prospect.
Zealand Pharma has reported more phase 2 data on its Roche-partnered amylin analog, linking the drug candidate to competitive weight loss but a lackluster effect on blood sugar.
A phase 2 celiac disease trial of argenx’s FB102 has hit its primary endpoint, delivering a boost to a drug candidate that the biotech acquired in its $2.2 billion takeover of Forte Biosciences.

Cadrenal Therapeutics, a heart-focused biotech that recently reached an agreement with the FDA on the design of a pivotal trial for its lead candidate, is now instead looking to offload its pipeline or potentially the entire company.
As always, if you know of layoffs occurring at a biotech, please reach out to the Fierce Biotech editorial team.

The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services announced the launch of a new program aimed at removing barriers that slow clinical development and transforming how clinical trials are designed and conducted.
Investment firm TCGX is expanding in Asia, raising $600 million to funnel into biotechs emerging from a burgeoning drug discovery hotspot.
Cerevance's oral non-dopaminergic therapy has redeemed itself by improving both motor and non-motor symptoms in a phase 3 Parkinson's disease study.

Atsena Therapeutics has reported evidence of efficacy in a clinical trial of an eye disease gene therapy, encouraging the biotech to forge ahead with a study that could support a filing for approval in 2028.
Matchpoint Therapeutics has aced its series B round, serving up $150 million to advance the Sanofi-backed biotech’s pipeline of precision covalent medicines.
MimiVax has reports a phase 2b miss in newly diagnosed glioblastoma patients, but remains positive about a significant survival benefit in a subset of patients 65 years and under.
The Fierce Biotech Fundraising Tracker records venture capital rounds of $50 million or more secured by biotechs.
The Bay Area biotech is discontinuing all clinical development activities and implementing a "substantial reduction in workforce."
Stryker veteran Spencer Stiles will take up the chief executive role as its former CEO Kevin Lobo will move into the boardroom.
Big Pharma-backed Nuvig Therapeutics has halted one of the two trials for its sole clinical asset after determining the program wouldn’t be able to advance quickly enough.

papers.summary: Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 07 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-026-01315-8 When newsroom artificial intelligence (AI) engages in emotional packaging, it changes how a story feels, shaping whether people approach, trust and share it. As these systems are designed and deployed, AI and behavioural researchers should work together to test whether emotional packaging helps accurate information reach readers, and whether it deepens division.

papers.title: Characterizing the role of reasoning tokens in large language models as state over tokens
papers.summary: Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 07 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-026-01303-y When large language models ‘reason’ about a problem, they might still solve it differently from what their reasoning transcript suggest. In this Perspective, Levy et al. describe how one can start investigating the role of these reasoning tokens.

papers.title: Shifting from knowledge retrieval to evidence exploration and synthesis
papers.summary: Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 01 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-026-01313-w Biomedical discovery has entered an era in which the limiting resource is no longer data, but our ability to integrate and interpret evidence. DeepEvidence, a new deep research agent, goes beyond retrieving facts and constructs explicit representations of scientific evidence.

papers.title: Large language models discover complementary heuristics for combinatorial optimization
papers.summary: Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 01 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-026-01307-8 Huatian Gong and colleagues developed LACE, a large language model-based framework that designs optimization algorithms. It builds a verified problem contract, then evolves a portfolio of complementary heuristics that together solve problems that no single method can handle.

papers.title: Towards foundation-style models for energy-frontier heterogeneous neutrino detectors via self-supervised pretraining
papers.summary: Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 30 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-026-01309-6 Alonso-Monsalve et al. demonstrate that self-supervised pretraining helps deep learning models to interpret complex neutrino detector events, improving classification, reconstruction and data efficiency while enabling transfer across different neutrino detector technologies.

papers.title: Regional climate risk assessment from climate models using probabilistic machine learning
papers.summary: Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 28 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-026-01308-7 A generative AI framework called GenFocal is introduced for climate downscaling, producing realistic fine-scale weather from coarse projections and improving regional risk estimates of compound extremes such as heatwaves and tropical cyclones.

papers.title: Task-structured modularity emerges in artificial networks and aligns with brain architecture
papers.summary: Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 28 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-026-01306-9 Wu et al. show that neural networks learning multiple tasks organize into specialized modules, particularly under capacity constraints. Incremental multitask learning strengthens this modularity and produces architectures resembling brain networks.

papers.title: Minute-scale training for microrobot navigation
papers.summary: Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 28 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-026-01305-w A vectorized simulator and structured reward framework enable microrobot navigation policies to be trained within minutes and transferred without retraining across robots and environments.
